area: CSV and input integrity (parseCSV and every consumer in exceptions.js and app.js)
summary: The committed data is clean and the dashboard handles it correctly: 8 of 8 tests pass and there are 10 alerts. Real exports are different. parseCSV (exceptions.js:22-34) splits every line on every comma. It ignores quotes, turns any value that looks like a number into a Number (IDs included), and keeps a blank cell as "". Nothing downstream checks columns, types, ranges, references, duplicates or dates. I ran 66 cases through the real functions (node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs) and 58 fail; 10 browser cases (node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.browser.mjs) and 9 fail. The confirmed outcomes fall into four groups. (1) Missed alerts. A quoted comma in a task, pasture or category name drops that row's alert: the booster overdue, the over-plan grazing and the over-budget alerts all disappear. A level written as "11.8%", "ERR" or "NaN" passes as OK. Writing the status as "Open" hides every health alert. A renamed level column turns off all water level alerts. A duplicated EID weigh-in erases the Heifers group alert. A September actual not yet entered hides Fuel being 20% over. (2) False alarms. A blank level becomes "Down to % full" (critical). Excel blank rows (,,,) create a critical alert for a tank with no name. A -999 sensor code becomes "Dropped 1079 points". A blank planned_graze_days becomes "Day 18 of a -day plan". A move left without an out_date shows the yearlings in two pastures, one of them "15 days over". (3) Crashes that blank the whole report with no error message. These come from an Excel blank row in moves or weights, an animal with one weigh-in, a pasture_id that is not in pastures.csv, a trailing space in an ID, a group named "2025", and a groups.csv with no group named "Yearlings" (app.js hard-codes it, so the exception table never renders). (4) Misleading all-clear. An empty water export shows "Water tanks OK 0 of 0", and a tank missing from the export simply vanishes. Re-saving water.csv in US Excel (M/D/YYYY dates) replaces the real T2 low-tank and T4 leak critical alerts with 8 identical "No reading for 516 hours" alerts. Handled correctly: a UTF-8 BOM (trim removes it), CRLF and LF line endings, unsorted rows, exact duplicate water rows, spaces around numbers, an extra trailing column. The README line "To use real data, replace the CSVs with exports in the same columns" is not safe today.
trace:
Source to screen, as the code is written:
1. app.js:221 fetches each data/<f>.csv and calls .text(). The browser strips a UTF-8 BOM, and in node parseCSV's text.trim() strips it too.
2. parseCSV (exceptions.js:22-34) works in this order:
   - trim() the whole text, then split(/\r?\n/). CR-only files become one line.
   - The header is split(",") with no trim and no quote handling, and is not checked against the expected columns.
   - lines.filter(Boolean) drops only truly empty lines, so ",,," and "   " become rows.
   - Each line is split(","): a quoted comma shifts every later column, quotes stay in the text, extra fields are dropped and missing fields become "".
   - Each value v: if v !== "" and !isNaN(+v) it becomes Number(v), so "007"→7, "0x10"→16, "1e3"→1000, "Infinity"→Infinity and "   "→0. Otherwise the raw string is kept: "", "11.8%", "ERR", "NaN", "$3,000", "\"P3".
   - There are no checks on schema, types, ranges, references or duplicates.

Consumers:
- Water. waterStatus (:39-52) groups by tank_id and sorts with time.localeCompare, which is a string sort: an M/D/YYYY time mis-orders and a numeric time throws. It takes the last row and computes silentHours = (as_of − last.time)/h; an invalid date gives NaN, which is never "silent". drop24h = dayAgo.level_pct − last.level_pct, and "" coerces to 0. findExceptions (:101-116) then applies, in order: silent ≥24 h → serious, and the level is not judged; drop ≥30 → critical; level <25 → critical; level <40 → warning. JS comparison makes "" act as 0 (a false critical) and makes "ERR", "NaN" and "11.8%" act as NaN (always false, so the tank passes silently). The subject reads pName[pasture_id] ("undefined" if the pasture is unknown) plus whoIsThere from grazing. On screen: an exceptions table row through innerHTML, the tile "Water tanks OK" = tanks − tanks with any Water alert, and the chart header `${t.level}%` (shows "ERR%").
- Grazing. grazingStatus (:54-61) takes moves with a falsy out_date (blank = current) and does byId[pasture_id].name, which throws when the pasture is unknown or the ID has a space. days(in_date, as_of date) minus planned_graze_days ("" → 0) > 0 → serious "Day N of a P-day plan"; ≥ −2 → warning.
- Gain. gainStatus (:64-80) groups by tag (Number or string) and sorts with date.localeCompare. It takes the last two rows: with one row b is undefined and it throws; with two rows on the same date it divides by 0 (±Infinity or NaN). A group's animals are matched by exact equality against groups.csv, so an unknown group is silently dropped, and a falsy target ("" or 0) skips the group. Group avg < 0.8·target → serious. Otherwise animals < 0.5·target → warning listing the coerced tags; the subject uses g.group.toLowerCase(), which throws for a numeric group.
- Health. Requires status === "open" exactly and a truthy next_due. days(as_of date, next_due): <0 → serious, ≤7 → warning, NaN → nothing. A non-ISO date parses as local time and gives fractional days.
- Budget. budgetStatus (:82-89) does `c.budget += r.budget; c.actual += r.actual`, which concatenates strings when a cell is "" or text. pct = (actual − budget)/budget: >10% → serious with the $variance, >5% → warning. NaN gives nothing; a budget of 0 gives Infinity.
- Meta. d.meta[0].as_of throws when there is no row.
- app.js startup has no error handling. Any throw in findExceptions leaves the page showing only the static headings. tiles() runs before exceptionsTable() and requires a group literally named "Yearlings". waterMultiples requires every tank to have a reading in the last 7 days, and when it throws, grazing, gain, budget and rules are never drawn.

findings.title: parseCSV is not a CSV parser: quoted commas shift columns, quotes and escaped quotes stay in the text, CR-only and fully quoted exports break
findings.location: exceptions.js:22-34 (lines 23, 24, 26); README.md 'To use real data, replace the CSVs with exports in the same columns'; scripts/generate_data.py:108-112 writes with csv.writer, which quotes such fields, so the repo's own writer and reader disagree
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs (cases CSV-01..CSV-08); node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.browser.mjs (B-09). Minimal case: parseCSV('a,b,c\n"x, y",2,3') gives [{"a":"\"x","b":" y\"","c":2}]. findExceptions with health row: Yearlings,"Booster vaccine, 2nd round",2026-06-02,2026-09-15,open
findings.expected: CSV-01: serious | Yearlings: Booster vaccine, 2nd round | Overdue by 15 days (due 2026-09-15). CSV-02: serious | Yearlings in Sand Hills, east | Day 24 of a 21-day plan (3 days over). CSV-03: serious | Fuel, diesel | 25% over season to date ($600). CSV-05: subject Cows: Check "bad eye" calves. CSV-07: critical Down to 11.8% full, no crash.
findings.actual: CSV-01/02/03/04/06/08: "(no alerts)". CSV-05: "warning|Cows: \"Check \"\"bad eye\"\" calves\"|Due in 3 days (2026-10-03)". CSV-07: "THROWS TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'localeCompare')". B-09 (committed data, P3 renamed "Sand Hills, east"): header "Example Ranch (fictional), 1200 east\"480400600700200 acres in 8 pastures"; chips "Grazing (0)" (the Yearlings over-plan alert is gone); chart header "T3 \"Sand Hills".
findings.consequence: Real exports quote any field that contains a comma. One such field silently removes the alert for that row: an overdue vaccination, a group grazing past plan, or an over-budget category simply isn't shown. A fully quoted export (common from accounting and sensor tools) silences the health alerts or crashes the page.
findings.regression_test: assert.deepEqual(parseCSV('a,b,c\n"x, y","say ""hi""",3'), [{a:'x, y', b:'say "hi"', c:3}]); assert.deepEqual(parseCSV('a,b\r1,2'), [{a:1,b:2}]). Using the CSV-01 fixture, findExceptions includes {severity:'serious', subject:'Yearlings: Booster vaccine, 2nd round', problem:'Overdue by 15 days (due 2026-09-15)'}; 15 = Sep 15 to Sep 30, counted on a calendar.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace line.split(',') with a small RFC 4180 state-machine tokenizer (quoted fields, "" escapes, commas and newlines inside quotes, CRLF/LF/CR) and trim header names. About 35 lines, no dependency. Add a round-trip test: a row written with Python csv.writer must parse back to the same values. Reword the README sentence to state the accepted format.

findings.title: An animal with a single weigh-in (bought or tagged mid-season) crashes gainStatus and blanks the page
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs (CSV-17); node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.browser.mjs (B-02: committed data plus 'Y151,Yearlings,2026-09-15,700')

findings.expected: CSV-43: no 'Down to % full'; treat the cell as a missing reading. CSV-44: Fuel still flagged, since Jun-Aug is 8,640 against 7,200 (20% over), or a 'September actual missing' flag. CSV-45: Fuel 21% over ($1,512), from 2592+3120+3000 = 8712 against 7200. CSV-46: no '-day plan' alert. CSV-48: no alerts (Y2-Y4 at 2.105 against 2.0). B-08: head 330, or heifers marked unknown.
findings.actual: CSV-13: "critical|Tank T1 (North Flat)|Dropped 80 points in 24 hours, now %". CSV-43: "critical|Tank T1 (North Flat)|Down to % full". CSV-44: only "serious|Repairs|25% over season to date ($1,800)"; Fuel is gone. CSV-45: "serious|Fuel|2700324931% over season to date ($259,231,193,400)". CSV-46: "serious|Cows in South Divide|Day 18 of a -day plan (18 days over)". CSV-48: "serious|Yearlings|-1.49 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 2.0 target". B-07 tile: "SPEND VS BUDGET / +2.715256118778953e+22% / $24,002,864,090,005,946,000,000,000 of $88,400". B-08 tile: "HEAD ON GRASS / 180150".
findings.consequence: The usual mid-month budget state (current month not yet booked) hides a category that is 20% over, while the headline tile shows +2.7e22%. A sensor gap sends a crew on a 'go now' water call to a tank that may be full. One missing scale weight puts a small group on the serious gain list. Absurd figures in front of an employer undercut the portfolio's credibility.
findings.regression_test: CSV-43 fixture: no alert's problem matches /now %|Down to % full/. Committed data with Sep Fuel actual blank: Budget alerts include Fuel (Jun-Aug 8,640 against 7,200 = 20%, worked by hand) or a missing-value flag. budgetStatus([{category:'F',budget:2400,actual:''},{category:'F',budget:2400,actual:2928}]): typeof actual is 'number'. CSV-48 fixture: no Gain alerts.
findings.proposed_fix: Load each file against a typed schema. Numeric columns become Number or null (blank), never ''. Consumers handle null explicitly. Water: a null latest level gives a serious 'no valid reading since <time>' alert and is excluded from the drop calculation. Gain: exclude the animal and report 'missing weight'. Budget: compare only months that have an actual, or emit 'Fuel: September actual not entered'. Grazing: a missing plan gives a warning 'no planned graze days for P7'. Tiles: sum only finite numbers.

findings.title: Non-numeric, non-finite and out-of-range readings pass as OK or become nonsense alerts
findings.location: exceptions.js:30 (isNaN check keeps '11.8%', 'ERR', 'NaN' as strings; 'Infinity' becomes Infinity), :49, :109-115, :88 (budget 0 gives Infinity); app.js:47, :55, :82
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs (CSV-49..CSV-56); node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.browser.mjs (B-06: committed T2 latest reading set to ERR)
findings.expected: CSV-50: critical Down to 11.8% full, or a load error. CSV-51/52: a Water alert for each affected tank (reading unusable). CSV-53: a sensor-fault alert, not a leak. CSV-54: no leak alert (140 is not a real level). CSV-56: wording in money, not 'Infinity%'. B-06: '3 need a look'.
findings.actual: CSV-50/51/52/55: "(no alerts)". CSV-53: "critical|Tank T1 (North Flat)|Dropped 1079 points in 24 hours, now -999%". CSV-54: "critical|Tank T1 (North Flat)|Dropped 40 points in 24 hours, now 100%". CSV-49: "serious|Yearlings|-5.09 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 2.0 target". CSV-56: "serious|Hay|Infinity% over season to date ($500)". B-06: tile "WATER TANKS OK / 6 of 8 / 2 need a look"; chart header "T2 WindmillERR%"; the T2 critical row is gone.
findings.consequence: If a gateway appends '%' or reports ERR/NaN for a tank at 11.8%, the page says that tank is fine, and the tile counts it OK. That is a misleading all-clear on the one tank that needs a truck today. A -999 fault code or a 140% spike sends someone to fix a 'leak' at a full tank.
findings.regression_test: CSV-51 fixture (T2 latest 'ERR'): at least one Water alert whose subject starts with 'Tank T2'. CSV-53 fixture: no alert matching /Dropped|-999%/ and at least one alert for T1. CSV-56 fixture: a Hay alert whose problem does not contain 'Infinity'.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate level_pct as a finite number from 0 to 100 (strip a trailing '%'), weight_lbs > 0, and budget >= 0. An invalid latest reading produces a serious 'sensor reported "ERR" at <time>' alert and is excluded from level and drop logic. A budget of 0 with spend reads '$500 spent with no budget line'.

findings.title: No column checks: a renamed, misspelled or space-padded header silently turns a rule off
findings.location: exceptions.js:24 (header split with no trim and no validation); consumers read r.level_pct, h.status and d.meta[0].as_of directly (:47, :141, :95)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs (CSV-09, CSV-24, CSV-25, CSV-31). On committed data with header 'level_pct ' (trailing space), a scratch probe gives 8 alerts instead of 10.
findings.expected: A load error naming the file and the missing column, or, for 'level_pct ', a trimmed header with normal behaviour (T2 critical 11.8%).
findings.actual: CSV-24 (column 'level'): "(no alerts)". CSV-09: "(no alerts)". CSV-25 (no status column): "(no alerts)". CSV-31: "THROWS TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'as_of')". Committed data with 'level_pct ': LOST "critical|Water|Tank T2 (Windmill)|Down to 11.8% full" and "critical|Water|Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now)|Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10%"; NEW "serious|Water|Tank T6 (Cedar Draw)|No reading for 42 hours; last level undefined%".
findings.consequence: A vendor export that calls the column 'level' or 'Level %' disables every low-tank and leak alert, and the page still looks normal: a misleading all-clear on water. A health export without a status column hides all vaccination alerts.
findings.regression_test: Load water text with header 'tank_id,pasture_id,time,level': the loader throws an Error whose message includes 'water.csv' and 'level_pct'. Header 'level_pct ' (trailing space): T2 critical 'Down to 11.8% full' is still reported.
findings.proposed_fix: Declare REQUIRED columns per file, trim header names, and on a missing column throw (or collect) a 'Data' exception that is shown at the top of the report.

CSV-20: warning 'Under 1.0 lbs/day: 0x10' (0x10 = 20/57 = 0.351; group average (0.351 + 3×2.105)/4 = 1.667 ≥ 1.6, so no group alert). findings.consequence: The pull list names the wrong animal (the crew looks for tag 16 instead of 0x10, or 7 instead of 007). Two animals merge into one with -Infinity gain. A ranch that names groups by calf-crop year ('2025') gets a blank page. A group 19 days past its plan is reported as 'move in 1 day', because pasture 01 is judged against pasture 1's 30-day plan.

Keep every *_id, tag, group, name, task, category, status and date as a trimmed string. Update the existing 'CSV parsing keeps text as text and numbers as numbers' test, which currently enshrines blanket coercion.

findings.title: app.js hard-codes a group named 'Yearlings': real data without one hides the whole exception report
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.browser.mjs (B-03: 'Yearlings' renamed 'Steers' in groups, weights, moves and health)
findings.expected: findExceptions succeeds on this data, so all 10 exception rows are shown.

findings.title: A tank silent for more than 7 days crashes the water charts and every section drawn after them
findings.location: app.js:90-93 (rows filtered to the last 7 days; last.time on undefined), :225 (render order)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.browser.mjs (B-04: T6 rows after 2026-09-20 removed from committed water.csv)

findings.actual: B-04: page errors ["Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'time')"]; 10 exception rows, including "Serious Water Tank T6 (Cedar Draw) No reading for 240 hours; last level 100%"; but 0 water charts, grazing chart false, gain chart false, 0 budget table rows, 0 rules rows.

findings.title: No list of expected tanks: an empty water export, or a tank missing from the export, gives an all-clear
findings.location: exceptions.js:39-52 (tanks come only from rows present); app.js:46, :55 (tile)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs (CSV-29, CSV-30); node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.browser.mjs (B-05: water.csv header only)
findings.expected: An alert for each known tank with no reading in 24 hours, and a 'no water data loaded' alert when the file is empty.
findings.actual: CSV-29: "(no alerts)". CSV-30 (T6 rows removed from committed data): Water alerts are only T2 and T4; T6 is gone. B-05: tile "WATER TANKS OK / 0 of 0 / 0 need a look", chips "Water (0)", 7 exception rows.
findings.consequence: The silent-sensor rule only catches a sensor that stopped inside the exported window. If the gateway exports only recent days, or is itself down and exports nothing, the page tells the manager water is fine. Water is the alert that most directly protects animal welfare.
findings.regression_test: With a tank registry (T1-T8) and a header-only water.csv: 8 serious 'No reading' alerts. With T6 rows removed from committed data: a serious alert for T6.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tanks.csv (tank_id, pasture_id), or a tank column in pastures.csv. Have waterStatus iterate the registry and treat a tank with no rows as silent. Add a 'water file has no readings' alert. Likewise flag a group that has a target but no weigh-ins.

findings.title: A duplicated weigh-in for one animal (EID double read) erases or downgrades the group's gain alert
findings.location: exceptions.js:68-70 (last two rows on the same date: divide by 0), :77 (average absorbs NaN or Infinity), :129
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs (CSV-32). A scratch probe on committed data appends 'H001,Heifers,2026-09-15,1169' (and separately ',1170').
findings.expected: CSV-32: serious | Heifers | 0.70 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 1.0 target (each heifer 40/57 = 0.702 < 0.8). On committed data the Heifers serious alert stays.
findings.actual: CSV-32: "(no alerts)". Committed data plus one duplicate H001 row: LOST "serious|Gain|Heifers|0.44 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 1.0 target"; NEW "warning|Gain|32 heifers|Under 0.5 lbs/day: H002, H004, ...". A duplicate weight of 1170 gives the same result.
findings.consequence: EID scale heads routinely double-read a tag. One such row removes a group-wide serious gain problem entirely (when no individual is under 50%), or turns it into a lower-severity per-animal list.
findings.regression_test: CSV-32 fixture: exactly one alert, severity serious, subject 'Heifers', problem '0.70 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 1.0 target'.
findings.proposed_fix: Deduplicate weights by (tag, date): keep the last row and report the duplicate count. Require from < to. Exclude non-finite ADG from averages and report it.

findings.title: Other duplicate and contradictory records are not detected: false budget warnings, double alerts, a group shown in two pastures
findings.location: exceptions.js:55 (last duplicate pasture wins), :84-87, :97, :140-147, :56 (several open moves allowed per group)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs (CSV-33..CSV-37). A scratch probe on committed data with budget.csv rows appended twice gives 'Fuel 21% over season to date ($4,080)'.
findings.expected: CSV-33: no alerts (9,600 against 10,000 = 4.2%). CSV-34: a duplicate-ID error, or the 21-day alert. CSV-35/36: one alert. CSV-37: only the Sand Hills alert, or a 'two open moves' error. Doubled budget: $2,040.
findings.actual: CSV-33: "warning|Fuel|7% over season to date". CSV-34: "(no alerts)". CSV-35: two identical "serious|Yearlings: Booster vaccine|Overdue by 15 days" rows. CSV-36: two identical Heifers rows. CSV-37: "serious|Yearlings in South Divide|Day 36 of a 21-day plan (15 days over) || serious|Yearlings in Sand Hills|Day 24 of a 21-day plan (3 days over)".
findings.consequence: A re-export creates false budget warnings and doubles the dollar figures. A forgotten out_date shows the yearlings in two pastures and '15 days over' in one they already left, which could send a crew to move cattle that aren't there.
findings.regression_test: CSV-33 fixture: no alerts, or a duplicate error. CSV-37 fixture: no alert with subject 'Yearlings in South Divide' (Aug 25 to Sep 30 = 36 days, counted by hand, shows where the false figure comes from).
findings.proposed_fix: Check key uniqueness per file (pasture_id, group, (month, category), (group, task, next_due), at most one open move per group) and report Data warnings. Drop exact duplicates.

findings.title: Dates are never validated; non-ISO formats (as US Excel re-saves them) mis-sort or shift by the time zone
findings.location: exceptions.js:36 (new Date on raw strings), :43 and :68 (string localeCompare sort), :58, :95, :142
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/csv.repro.mjs (CSV-38, CSV-39, CSV-40, CSV-40b, CSV-41, CSV-42). Scratch probe5.mjs run with TZ=America/Chicago rewrites the committed dates as M/D/YYYY.
findings.expected: CSV-40b: T2 critical (11.8%) and T4 critical (leak) still present, and T6 the only silent tank. CSV-41: 'Overdue by 15 days'. CSV-38/39/42: a load error naming the date.
findings.actual: CSV-40b: eight alerts "serious|Tank T1..T8|No reading for 516 hours; last level ..." and no T2 or T4 critical. CSV-40: "serious|Tank T1 (North Flat)|No reading for 504 hours; last level 80%". CSV-41: "Overdue by 14.791666666666666 days (due 9/15/2026)". Chicago probe with M/D dates in health and moves: "Day 23.791666666666668 of a 21-day plan (2.791666666666668 days over)" and "Due in 3.2083333333333335 days". CSV-38: "(no alerts)". CSV-39: "warning|Cows: Pinkeye check|Due in 1 day (2026-09-31)" (V8 rolls the date to Oct 1). CSV-42: "(no alerts)".
findings.consequence: Opening water.csv in Excel and saving it, the most likely thing a manager does with a CSV, makes every tank look silent and buries the real leak and the low tank under eight identical alerts. US-format due dates print '14.79 days' for a Texas viewer. A mistyped month makes an overdue vaccination disappear.
findings.regression_test: CSV-40b: committed water.csv with times rewritten as M/D/YYYY H:MM gives critical T2 'Down to 11.8% full' and critical T4 'Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10%' (both checked by hand against data/water.csv rows), plus exactly one 'No reading' alert (T6). A health row with next_due '2026-13-15' gives a load error naming health.csv.
findings.proposed_fix: Parse dates and times once at load with explicit patterns (YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, optionally M/D/YYYY[ H:MM]) into numeric timestamps, validating day-of-month. Sort numerically. Report anything else as a Data alert naming the file, row and value.

checked_ok: UTF-8 BOM. String.prototype.trim removes U+FEFF, so parseCSV('﻿a,b\n1,2') gives key lengths [1, 1]. OK-01, with a BOM prepended to all 8 committed files, prints 'same 10 alerts' and MATCH.
CRLF and LF line endings. The committed CSVs are CRLF (grep -c $'\r' data/water.csv = 954) and split(/\r?\n/) handles them. OK-02 (LF against CRLF): 'same 10 alerts', MATCH.

Blank lines and trailing newlines. parseCSV('a,b
1,2

3,4') gives [{a:1,b:2},{a:3,b:4}] (probe1). Trailing newlines are trimmed.

Extra fields. A row with too many fields still raises the right alert: OK-03 gives 'critical|Tank T2 (North Flat)|Down to 11.8% full', MATCH. The extra field is silently dropped. A trailing comma on every committed water row also gives the same 10 alerts (probe3).

Unsorted rows. Water and weights are sorted per tank and per tag. OK-04 (committed water reversed): same alerts, MATCH. Committed weights reversed: same alerts, only the slow-tag list order reverses ('Y132, Y129, ...').
Exact duplicate water rows are harmless. OK-05 (committed water.csv doubled): 'same 10 alerts', MATCH.
Spaces around numbers. ' 11.8 ' becomes 11.8: OK-06 gives critical 'Down to 11.8% full', MATCH.
Numeric category names. A budget category like 6100 works: OK-07 gives 'serious|6100|25% over season to date ($600)', MATCH.
Intentional blanks. A blank out_date marks the current move, and a blank next_due on a done task is skipped: OK-08 gives '(no alerts)', MATCH.

Committed data baseline. node --test tests/exceptions.test.mjs: 'pass 8, fail 0'. The headless Chromium baseline (B-00) shows 10 exception rows, 5 tiles, 8 water charts, 7 budget table rows and 12 rules rows, with no page errors.

Time zone. The repro gives the same totals under TZ=UTC, America/Chicago and Asia/Tokyo (66 cases: 8 MATCH, 58 MISMATCH each time). Committed ISO date-only and as_of strings give whole-day counts in all three. Only non-ISO input shifts (CSV-41).
